decisions.reason: The accent must derive its proportions from the Hero V, so the revised wider and more substantial Hero V geometry necessarily changes its derivation basis.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
One thing I'm realizing from this latest round is that I don't think the answer is making the V taller and more slender.

When I look back at the reference image I shared, what continues to resonate with me isn't necessarily its height—it's its presence.

It has confidence. It occupies space. It feels substantial without feeling heavy.

I think the newer concepts may have become a little too narrow in pursuit of elegance. While I appreciate the refinement, I actually find myself drawn back to a V with a bit more visual authority and width.

To me, elegance isn't coming from making the letter increasingly slender. It's coming from achieving the right balance between confidence and restraint.

I'd love to keep exploring within this family, but with a little more emphasis on presence rather than elongation. I think there may be a sweet spot where the V feels composed, confident, and timeless without becoming either bulky or delicate.

value_updates.derivation_source: revised Hero V geometry emphasizing greater width, visual authority, and substantial presence rather than tall, slender elongation

decisions.reason: The closing V is explicitly derived from the Hero V geometry, so its geometric derivation must follow the newly selected wider and more authoritative proportions.
